name: Chloe Olsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary workday like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and fit timber stairs and roof details on building sites. The vocational trade certificate got me into carpentry, and my pay is above the usual rate because I take difficult flights and awkward heights, though I'm not the site manager. I like a clean joint; a plan that ignores uneven concrete makes the day longer.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is home like, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works in a school office, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We've saved nine months of expenses and there are plenty of similar construction jobs nearby. I use AI now and then to check a timber tally or turn rough notes into a list, but I don't send the list before measuring the site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell our stair crew the little AI helper can make a tidy materials list, but it can't tell whether the landing is level. We can use it for sums and keep fitting the stairs ourselves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I earn more than many carpenters because I take difficult stair and roof jobs, and we've saved nine months of expenses. My partner's school office wage helps with the mortgage and two children, so a small paperwork change feels manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll carry on fitting the arts centre stairs and use the chatbot now and then to check a timber tally, as I already do. My partner and I will add a small new payment to the mortgage from my next run of higher-paid jobs if the school costs leave room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. A faster tally is welcome, but I am paid for the fit and finish you can touch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did the plan fail on a stair?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On the last landing, the plan showed a clean right angle and the poured concrete didn't give us one. I scribed the first tread to the actual edge before cutting the rest.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would fund an extra mortgage payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra payment would come from future site wages after our ordinary bills. The nine months already saved stays separate, so we can still cover a gap between contracts.

say: **Material tallies** may get quicker without changing who fits stairs.
**Concrete edges** still need a carpenter's measurement before timber is cut.
think: My **higher site wage** and nine-month reserve keep this mild change manageable.
The **mortgage and children** still shape how much spare pay we have.
do: **Fit** arts centre stairs and measure each landing before cutting treads.
**Pay extra** toward mortgage from new higher-paid jobs if school costs allow.
feel: **Calm** about a modest tool improvement and continued site wages.
S0.quote: I scribed the first tread to the actual edge before cutting the rest.
fieldNote: She uses AI **now and then** for material tallies, but her stair fitting depends on measured concrete.
The proposed **extra mortgage payment** comes from future higher-paid work, conditional on school costs; existing savings remain available.

steps.text: Fit arts centre stairs and measure landings before cutting treads
Pay extra mortgage from new site wages if school costs allow

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the site crew planning and buying will change before a robot walks up our stairs. If an AI program draws the tread list, I still want the person fitting it to check every rise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My paid fitting work looks safe as office tasks change, and plenty of nearby contractors still hire trades. I worry a rushed digital schedule could leave me waiting for timber when the school office closes and my partner needs help with the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep a record of three actual stair rises against the digital tread list on the next arts centre flight. If the contractor adopts the new AI planning screen, I'll ask a colleague who uses it daily to show me its correction controls, then try those controls on one finished flight before trusting the next order.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about being rushed by a screen, though not about my wage vanishing soon. I can try a tool when somebody shows that it catches mistakes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do if a tread list is wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd mark the stair height on the drawing and call the timber yard before it cuts the wrong pieces. A short call to the timber yard is cheaper than remaking a whole stair flight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the new screen safely?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would try the corrected list against a flight we've already built, where we know the actual measurements. If it matches the timber we used, I'll allow it on the next live order with a manual check.

say: **AI planning** may draw tread lists before robots fit stairs.
**Stair rises** still need checking by the carpenter on site.
think: My own **fitting wage** looks secure during office changes.
A rushed **digital schedule** could waste paid time and disrupt our childcare handover.
do: **Record** three actual stair rises against the arts centre tread list.
**Learn** AI correction controls from colleague if new planner is adopted.
**Trial** controls on a finished flight before the next live order.
feel: **Uneasy** about rushed orders while continued fitting work feels secure.
S1.quote: A short call to the timber yard is cheaper than remaking a whole stair flight.
fieldNote: She is willing to learn **new AI controls** only if the contractor adopts them and a known flight proves useful.
The current risk is **wasted time** and childcare strain, not a predicted loss of her wage.

steps.text: Record three stair rises against arts centre digital tread list
Learn adopted AI planner controls from colleague on finished flight

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew AI by 2028 might design the stairs and book the timber, while capable robots around 2031 could fit a flight. We need the contractor's paid-work plan before anybody counts carpenters out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be about 48 when robots can do our physical fitting. Our nine months of savings and plenty of local builders buy us options, but a cut to my higher stair wage would still change the mortgage budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the site manager for the next two years of stair work and any real robot pilot dates. If a building survey course with a recognised certificate, funded fees and paid release is offered, I'll enrol and attend the classes; if our shifts are cut first, I'll apply to posted local carpentry vacancies that pay enough for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing the better-paid stair shifts, with enough savings to choose carefully. I want proof of the course and of the vacancy before making a move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your partner about the buffer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my partner the savings can bridge a gap, but they are not a replacement for my wage every month. We would look at the mortgage payment and school costs before accepting any unfunded course fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the survey course worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for the actual course start date, paid release hours and a qualification local firms accept. A free briefing is information; I would only count training once I enrol and go.

say: **2028 thinking AI** may design stairs before robots can fit them around 2031.
Carpenters need **paid-work plans** before site robots change staffing.
think: At about **48**, I could lose higher-paid stair shifts to robots.
Nine months of **savings** and local builders help, but mortgage costs remain.
do: **Ask** manager about stair workload and robot pilot dates.
**Enrol** in recognised survey course if funded fees, paid release and a real place are offered.
**Apply** after shift cuts to posted local carpentry jobs paying enough for mortgage.
feel: **Anxious** about possible income loss, with a buffer and options.
S2.quote: Our nine months of savings and plenty of local builders buy us options, but a cut to my higher stair wage would still change the mortgage budget.
fieldNote: Her **survey course** requires a real place, funded fees, a recognised certificate and paid release; a briefing is not enrolment.
Any employer change needs an **actual shift cut**, posted local vacancy and mortgage-covering pay despite her strong reserve.

steps.text: Ask manager about stair workload and robot pilot dates
Enrol in recognised survey course if funded fees, real place and paid release offered
Apply after shift cut to posted local carpentry job paying mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2031 will probably change drawings and orders first, then site robots around 2034 may handle a stair flight. Five years lets us test one installation and see what remains for a carpenter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At about 51 I would still want the higher wage, especially if the mortgage is not much smaller. The longer runway gives me time to learn building inspection on paid time, but I won't assume the contractor will pay without asking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll ask whether the contractor will fund a recognised building inspection course with paid time off for assessments. If it agrees in writing, I'll enrol next intake; meanwhile we'll add money from future higher-paid shifts to the mortgage so we have a smaller balance if hours fall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a possible cut, but five years is time to build another skill and reduce the loan. A robot trial should be measured in finished stairs, not minutes of demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should a robot trial measure?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the contractor to test a robot on a complete practice flight with an odd landing. I'd measure the rise and finish against the same safety checks we use for a person's work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much could you put toward the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner and I could add perhaps a hundred a month to the mortgage while I have the higher-paid shifts. The nine-month reserve is still for emergencies, and the extra payment stops if school expenses jump.

say: **2031 thinking AI** changes drawings before robots fit stairs around 2034.
A **complete practice flight** would test safety and finish before live site work.
think: At about **51**, a reduced stair wage could still hurt our mortgage budget.
Five years allows **paid training** and new loan payments if the employer agrees.
do: **Ask** contractor for recognised inspection course and paid assessment release.
**Enrol** next intake if course funding and paid release are written down.
**Pay extra** mortgage from future high-paid shifts while school costs permit.
feel: **Anxious** about possible wage cuts, with time for a second qualification.
S3.quote: A robot trial should be measured in finished stairs, not minutes of demonstration.
fieldNote: She ties **actual enrolment** to written course funding and paid release; a funding enquiry alone is not her training step.
Her **new mortgage payments** would use future shift wages and stop if school expenses jump, preserving the existing reserve.

steps.text: Ask contractor for written inspection course funding and paid release
Enrol in inspection course if written funding and paid release secured
Pay extra mortgage from future higher-paid shifts if school costs permit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI by 2036 can make the stair drawings, then capable robots around 2039 may do the fitting. A decade gives us time to see which nearby firms actually use them and where carpentry remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be about 56 when those robots arrive, with older children and hopefully a smaller mortgage. I cannot treat either a paid-off house or an inspection job as certain, but our savings give us room to plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep my stair safety certificate current and check local building inspection vacancies once a year. If a recognised part-time inspection course has a place and its fee fits after our mortgage payments, I'll enrol within the next year, then apply only to posted local inspection roles with pay and hours that suit our household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about a distant change to site work, interested in preparing without quitting a good wage. Ten years lets me ask for evidence instead of chasing a headline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make an inspection vacancy worthwhile?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd compare the advertised inspection wage to the actual mortgage payment and the hours to school pick-up. A site inspector title is no use if the weekly pay leaves our mortgage short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What site habit would you carry into inspection?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still inspect the joint with a ruler and ask who signed off the measurements. A computer drawing can carry an error for years if everyone assumes somebody else checked it.

say: **2036 thinking AI** changes drawings before robots fit stairs around 2039.
A decade allows **measured training** against real local vacancies.
think: At about **56**, the mortgage may be lower, but it is not guaranteed gone.
Our **strong reserve** supports planning while a new role remains uncertain.
do: **Keep** stair safety certificate current while continuing site work.
**Enrol** in recognised part-time inspection course if place and affordable fee exist.
**Apply** only to posted local inspection jobs with household-suitable pay and hours.
feel: **Uneasy** about distant job changes, with time to test alternatives.
S4.quote: A site inspector title is no use if the weekly pay leaves our mortgage short.
fieldNote: She considers **part-time training** only with a real place and affordable fee after mortgage costs.
She would seek **posted local inspection work** only if actual pay and hours suit the household, while maintaining her current trade.

steps.text: Keep stair safety certificate current while fitting sites
Enrol in recognised part-time inspection course if place and affordable fee exist
Apply after course to posted local inspection job with household-suitable pay and hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because robots around 2031 could cut the higher-paid stair work while our mortgage and children still need wages. A paid, recognised inspection course and honest site staffing figures would help me plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks the top step when a machine fits the whole flight. A stair robot can finish a beautiful flight that still has a dangerous final rise. Someone has to measure it before a family walks up.

headlineQuote: A stair robot can finish a beautiful flight that still has a dangerous final rise.
portrait: **Chloe**, 43, is a mid-level site carpenter with a vocational certificate and higher pay from difficult stair and roof jobs.
Her school-office partner and two children share a **mortgage** with her; the household has nine months of expenses saved.
She uses **AI now and then** and learns new controls after testing them against a completed stair flight.
Fast site robots make her **anxious** about her better-paid work; longer timelines favour conditional inspection training and new mortgage payments.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring stair-fitting robots around 2031 while mortgage payments still depend on her higher wages.
whatWouldHelp: A **paid, recognised inspection course** and honest site staffing figures would support a workable change.
